market_context.summary: Pre-open Monday; all equity prices below are the 2026-10-02 close, which is the freshest honest print with the market shut. The regime fact of the day is the shape of the curve rather than its level: the 2-year fell 10bp in one session to 4.78% while the 10-year moved 5bp to 5.24%, against an effective funds rate of 3.88%. That is the market pricing cuts from the front end while the long end holds a term premium, and with unemployment ticking 4.1% to 4.2% it is a labour-driven cut narrative rather than a growth-acceleration one. A 5.24% 10-year with funds at 3.88% is an unusual configuration and it is doing most of the work in this report - it is the stated cause of the 6% monthly gold pullback, the reason utilities stay pressured, and the tax on the financed discretionary demand behind LCII. The week is deliberately light: Q3 earnings season does not start until 2026-10-13, so ISM Services at 10:00 ET today and the FOMC September minutes on Wednesday are the only scheduled inputs before Delta reports Thursday. Week-ahead commentary names Treasury yields and oil as the primary drivers. Banks are notably rolling over into their own earnings - XLF -8.7% and JPM -9.3% off their highs - which against a front-end steepening points at credit rather than margin. No index, VIX, DXY, gold-futures or WTI level is stated anywhere in this report because every Yahoo-sourced quote failed with HTTP 429.

recommendations.thesis: Delta has beaten consensus EPS in each of the last four quarters - +4.4%, +10.7%, +0.5% and +10.5% - and goes into its 2026-10-09 Q3 print having given back 12.11% from its 90-day high, closing 84.09 on 2026-10-02 sitting exactly on its 50-day of 84.08 and still above its rising 20-day of 81.40 and well above its 200-day of 75.80. The mechanism is the setup rather than the story: a name with a four-for-four beat record and no analyst revision drift into it is being marked down with the broader tape, so the entry is into real moving-average support rather than at a discount invented off the last print, and the event that resolves it is four sessions away. RED TEAM: the earnings date was independently re-fetched and confirmed - DAL is on the finnhub calendar for 2026-10-09, before the open, consensus EPS 1.9868, so the validation block's 'not on the fetched calendar' warning is a false negative from a narrower fetch window and the dated catalyst stands. Conviction is cut 4 to 3 on the evidence, not the date: a 4-of-4 beat record is public and mechanical - most large caps beat - so it is close to no information about direction, and the one positioning item that is specific cuts both ways within itself.
recommendations.key_risk: The entire edge is one scheduled print four sessions out, so this gaps overnight either way and the 78.1 stop will not protect against a guidance cut - airlines move on forward capacity and fuel commentary far more than on the quarter reported. RED TEAM, and this is the material point: because the stop cannot function across an earnings gap, the published 2.35:1 overstates the trade. The 4.9 points of risk it is computed from is what the stop would contain in ordinary sessions, not what a guidance cut delivers at the open, so the true reward-to-risk is worse than the figure shown and unknowable in advance. Size is cut 3% to 2% for exactly that reason. The stop is also only 2.01 ATR from entry - it clears the 2.0 floor by half a percent and sits under the 2.5 ATR level where this report's stop-outs have clustered. Fuel is the live variable: week-ahead commentary names oil and Middle East developments as a primary driver of this week's price action, and a crude spike between now and Thursday damages the thesis before the print even happens.
recommendations.counter_argument: The strongest case against is insider behaviour: zero open-market purchases over the trailing six months against 14 sales totalling $44.3m net. That is genuinely unhelpful and is not argued away here - it is why this is sized at 2%. The partial answer is that executive sales at an airline that has run 10.7% off its 90-day low are weak evidence by construction, whereas the 4-of-4 beat record and a 90.6% bullish analyst share with revision_direction flat are measured and specific. The second case against is that the target at 94.5 sits within 1.3% of the 90-day high of 95.68, which is a demanding place to aim - stated plainly rather than hidden, and the reason half comes off into the print. The third, added by the red team: 'beats consensus four quarters running' is the single most widely known statistic about any company and roughly three in four large caps beat, so it cannot by itself support a 42% claim against a 29.9% break-even. What is left carrying the 12-point edge is the technical location - a mark-down into a rising 20-day and a flat 50-day with the long-term trend intact above a 75.80 200-day - which is a real but thin reason, and the honest score for it is 3.

recommendations.thesis: Update to the 2026-09-24 short: hold, levels unchanged, no new risk. XLU closed 39.83 on 2026-10-02 - the previous close, since the market is pre-open - below its 20-day of 40.97 and 50-day of 42.68 with the 50-day declining, so the downtrend the position was opened into is still intact. The mechanism is unchanged: at a 5.24% 10-year against a 3.88% effective funds rate the long end is carrying term premium rather than policy, and a regulated-utility cash flow stream is priced off the long end, so the front-end rally that dropped the 2-year 10bp last Thursday does nothing for the sector.
recommendations.key_risk: XLU closed only 2.05% above its own 90-day low of 39.03, so the easy part of this short is done and a mean-reversion bounce off that shelf would run through the 40.95 stop without the thesis changing. A long-end rally on weak labour data does real damage. This is also the fourth XLU recommendation in ten days, which prior_context flags as an anchoring warning rather than a conviction signal - it is published as an unchanged hold precisely because nothing new argues for it.
recommendations.counter_argument: The strongest case against is that the market is pricing cuts - the 2-year fell from 4.88% to 4.78% in a day and unemployment ticked 4.1% to 4.2% - and utilities historically lead on a cutting cycle. The answer is that utilities discount off the 10-year, not the 2-year, and the 10-year moved only 5bp to 5.24% on the same day; the curve steepened from the front, which is the configuration that leaves duration proxies unhelped.

data_quality_notes:
RESEARCH WAS NOT TRUNCATED. The research phase's notes run 06:03-07:14 ET and close with a RESEARCH COMPLETE block (research_minutes is null because those timestamps bound the phase from below rather than measuring it); it captured 12 rows across 7 distinct symbols, and synthesis takes the last row per symbol, so the five re-appended corrections are the live versions. All seven are published.

ONLY ONE OF THESE SEVEN ROWS IS NEW RISK: DAL (rank 3). Everything else is position management - one close (CCJ), one long-term reframe that attaches an invalidation the position never had (LCII), and four holds at unchanged levels (SVRA, GDX, SNX, XLU).

THE ERROR THE RESEARCH PHASE MADE AND CAUGHT, carried forward because it matters: a 06:17 diagnostic measured stop distance from the LAST PRINT instead of from ENTRY and concluded three stops were under 1.0 ATR, invoking the CLAUDE.md stop-out history for them. It acted on that before catching it at 06:55 - GDX had its stop widened 85.4 to 82.4 and SVRA 4.60 to 4.31, each 'fixing' a position that was correctly constructed, and the GDX change alone took the ratio from 2.28 to 1.52. Both are published at their ORIGINAL stops. I independently recomputed every ratio and ATR distance from the fetched OHLCV rather than trusting either set of figures; my numbers reproduce the corrected table exactly, including both floor failures below. What remains true from the original observation, stated correctly: SVRA and GDX each sit within ~0.85 ATR of their stops as of Friday's close, so each is roughly one ordinary session from being stopped. That is a live-risk fact and it is in each key_risk; it is not evidence a stop was set too tight.

TWO PUBLISHED IDEAS FAIL A FLOOR AND ARE DISCLOSED RATHER THAN REPAIRED, because both are filled positions whose entry cannot be amended. SNX (rank 6): the 242.5 stop is 1.33 ATR from the 260 entry against a 2.00 ATR floor. It is unfixable - clearing 2.00 ATR needs a stop at or below 233.67, beneath the 90-day low of 234.025, which would drop the ratio to 1.38 and fail the reward-to-risk floor instead. LCII (rank 4): 1.75:1 against the 2.5 long_term floor measured from the 94.0 fill. Neither was repaired by moving a target, and no addition is recommended to either. If the enforce step demotes them to the watchlist on that basis, that is the correct outcome and must not be worked around.

RATIO CLUSTERING - worth naming: four of the five ratios with a stop land at 2.07, 2.08, 2.28 and 2.35 against a 2.0 swing floor. On a page of fresh ideas that pattern would be the signature of targets fitted to clear the bar. Here it is not: all four are open positions published at levels set on the day each was opened, between 2026-09-19 and 2026-10-02, and none was amended today. SVRA at 3.53 is the only one with real headroom. The reader should still treat a 2.07 as what it is - an idea that clears its floor by 3%.

CORRELATION: the long-end rate story drives XLU short, GDX long and the unfilled TLT short - one bet with three faces, and the research notes flagged it as such. Only two of the three are in today's recommendations, so the 3-idea cap is not breached, but XLU and GDX resolve on the same 10-year print in opposite directions. LCII is also rate-sensitive, though as a long it leans the opposite way to the XLU short rather than stacking with it. Energy was declined outright on portfolio grounds: XLE, DINO and the unfilled OXY already fill the cap at 3, and week-ahead commentary named oil a primary driver this week - so that is a real opportunity passed on, not an absence of one.

REPETITION: XLU is its 4th recommendation in 10 days and GDX its 3rd. Per prior_context that is an anchoring warning, not conviction. Both are published only as unchanged holds of existing positions - neither has a new catalyst, neither is added to, and that is said in each thesis. PFE (4x in 10 days) and XLE (3x) were deliberately NOT re-pitched because nothing changed; the same goes for EEM and DINO.

COVERAGE GAPS. No index, VIX, DXY, gold-futures or WTI quote exists today - every Yahoo chart-API leg of macro returned HTTP 429, so those levels are null rather than estimated, and no index or VIX figure appears anywhere in this report. No options-implied move for any name (Yahoo options API 401). No event-contract price for anything: events 'Fed' returns only multi-leg tennis parlays matching the substring inside 'Federico', and 'FEDDECISION', 'interest rate' and 'CPI' each return zero rows, so the four unfilled Fed/CPI contracts in the book are untouched and no implied probability is quoted. That is the single biggest gap and it is a tooling failure, not a market one. ISM Services at 10:00 ET today has no fetched consensus, so no intraday candidate was built on it - nothing intraday cleared the bar today and none was manufactured. Bank loan-loss provisioning went unchecked, which is the one fact that would have decided XLF/JPM; research named it the best-defined unfinished thread for tomorrow. BCC and KHC remain open longs with neither a stop nor an invalidation condition - both are on the watchlist rather than guessed at.

PRICES: every last_price is the 2026-10-02 close at 16:00 ET, age ~62 hours. The US equity market is closed and it is pre-open Monday, so that is the freshest honest equity price available - a closed market, not stale data.

RED TEAM (phase 2c). Cut 2 of 7, downgraded 3, pulled 1 target in, trimmed 1 size. Five remain.

CUT - GDX (was rank 5): the thesis names the 5.24% 10-year as the cause of the pullback and then offers nothing that changes it, so its own stated mechanism is still running against the position. Its claim that 'the uptrend off the 69.74 low is undamaged' is false on a longer fetch - 87.78 is below the 20-day 93.65, the 50-day 91.44 and the 200-day 91.10, -25.09% off a 117.175 400-day high. And the sole forward argument is inverted: an October seasonal PEAK in precious metals argues the top is in. Ratio and stop both cleared their floors; this was not an arithmetic cut.
CUT - SNX (was rank 6): the 1.33 ATR stop against a 2.00 floor makes the 2.08:1 an artifact, and the report's own repair arithmetic shows a floor-clearing stop drops it to 1.38:1 - by the test this phase exists to apply, the idea never cleared. Decisive on consistency: DINO is the same situation better constructed (1.85 ATR, 2.10:1) and was already kept on the watchlist, so SNX could not stay published. NEITHER CUT IS A CLOSE INSTRUCTION - both are open positions that stay managed at their existing levels; what was cut is their publication as recommendations.

DOWNGRADED - DAL 4 to 3: the earnings date is CONFIRMED (re-fetched independently: DAL 2026-10-09 bmo, consensus EPS 1.9868, so validation's earnings_date warn is a false negative from a narrow window, and the same fetch confirms the 10-13 bank cluster). The cut is on evidence quality - a 4-of-4 beat record is public and mechanical and roughly three in four large caps beat, so it cannot carry a 42% claim against a 29.9% break-even, and the single specific positioning item contains $44.3m of net insider selling inside the same bullet. Size trimmed 3% to 2% on a separate point: key_risk concedes the stop cannot function across an earnings gap, so the 2.35:1 is computed from a risk the trade does not actually bound and overstates it. Still the only new risk in the report, and the only idea here whose price is above its 200-day.
DOWNGRADED - SVRA 4 to 3 and TARGET PULLED IN 8.00 to 7.00: two of three evidence items are the same company press release under two kind labels, so conviction rested on two confirmations, not three. The 8.00 target had no stated basis and sat above every price in 400 sessions (range high 7.005); 7.00 is that high, an actual level. Ratio 3.53 to 2.20, still clear of the 2.0 floor, with the 4.60 stop untouched - the target moved IN, and no ratio anywhere in this report was rescued by moving a stop or pushing a target out.
